items.question: Tell me about a time you had to deliver a project under a tight deadline.
items.whyAsked: Checks how you plan, prioritise and own outcomes under pressure.
items.answer: We had a deadline once and the team worked hard and we finished it on time. It was stressful but it went fine in the end.
items.note: vague, no own role, no result

items.question: Tell me about a time you had to deliver a project under a tight deadline.
items.whyAsked: Checks how you plan, prioritise and own outcomes under pressure.
items.answer: In my internship we had a demo in five days. I split the work into must-haves and nice-to-haves with my lead, built the retrieval part myself, cut the analytics dashboard, and we demoed on time; the client signed for a pilot.
items.note: complete STAR with own actions and result

items.question: How would you design a retrieval-augmented chatbot over a product catalogue?
items.whyAsked: Checks practical understanding of RAG: chunking, retrieval, evaluation.
items.answer: I would use an LLM and a vector database and connect them.

items.question: How would you design a retrieval-augmented chatbot over a product catalogue?
items.whyAsked: Checks practical understanding of RAG: chunking, retrieval, evaluation.
items.answer: I'd split manuals into 500-token chunks with some overlap, embed them, store vectors in pgvector, retrieve the top 5 by cosine similarity plus a keyword search, and pass them to the model with an instruction to cite sources. I'd build a question set from real support tickets to measure answer accuracy and tune chunk size against it.

items.question: Walk me through the evaluation set you built at your internship.
items.whyAsked: Checks that you really did the work on your resume and can explain it.
items.answer: I made some questions and checked the answers.

items.question: Walk me through the evaluation set you built at your internship.
items.whyAsked: Checks that you really did the work on your resume and can explain it.
items.answer: I wrote 150 questions with the support team, each with an expected answer and source page. Every night a script ran them through the bot and scored exact facts; when accuracy was 71% I tested chunk sizes from 256 to 1024 and rewrote the prompt, which got it to 86% over two weeks.

items.question: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate.
items.whyAsked: Checks how you handle conflict and reach decisions.
items.answer: Yeah, that happens sometimes, we usually talk it out.

items.question: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate.
items.whyAsked: Checks how you handle conflict and reach decisions.
items.answer: My teammate wanted to fine-tune a model; I thought prompt changes would be enough. I suggested we each try for one day against the same 50 test questions. Prompting reached 84% versus 86% for fine-tuning at a fraction of the cost, so we shipped prompting and kept fine-tuning as a later option.

items.question: How do you make sure an API you build is reliable?
items.whyAsked: Checks testing, monitoring and error handling habits.
items.answer: I test it.

items.question: How do you make sure an API you build is reliable?
items.whyAsked: Checks testing, monitoring and error handling habits.
items.answer: I write integration tests against a real Postgres in CI, validate every input with a schema so bad requests get a 400 instead of a 500, add timeouts and retries for external calls, and log latency and errors per route so I can see regressions after a deploy.

items.question: Why do you want to work at Northwind Analytics?
items.whyAsked: Checks motivation and that you know what the company does.
items.answer: Because it is a good company and I want to learn.

items.question: What's the hardest bug you have fixed?
items.whyAsked: Checks debugging approach and persistence.
items.answer: Our chatbot sometimes answered from the wrong manual. I logged the retrieved chunks for failing questions and saw near-duplicate chunks from two product versions outranking the right one. I added the product version as a metadata filter before vector search, and wrong-manual answers dropped from about 9% to under 1%.
